summary: Explains supplying extra signatures via `--signature` or a `signatures` key in requirements.yml, and that GnuPG verification only applies to collections installed from a distribution server. Covers controlling how many signatures must pass with `--required-valid-signature-count` / GALAXY_REQUIRED_VALID_SIGNATURE_COUNT, including `all` and the `+` prefix.
questions: How do I add signature URLs for a collection in requirements.yml?
Does signature verification work for collections installed from git or a tarball?
How many signatures have to be valid for a collection install to succeed?
How do I require every signature to verify?
How do I make the install fail if no valid signatures are found?

answer_card.title: Extra signatures and required signature count
answer_card.answer_md:
Pass extra signatures on the CLI with `--signature URI`, or list them in `requirements.yml`:

```yaml
collections:
  - name: ns.coll
    version: 1.0.0
    signatures:
      - https://examplehost.com/detached_signature.asc
      - file:///path/to/local/detached_signature.asc
```

GnuPG verification only happens for collections from a distribution server; user signatures are ignored for git repos, source directories, and tarball URLs/paths.

By default one valid signature is enough. Change this with `--required-valid-signature-count` or `GALAXY_REQUIRED_VALID_SIGNATURE_COUNT`; use `all` to require every signature, and prefix with `+` (e.g. `+all`, `+1`) to fail when no valid signatures are found.
